content:
## First, one correction before the manifests

The task says "Use ACK S3 CRDs (`s3.aws.upbound.io`)" — those two things are not the same thing, and you have to pick one:

- `s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1` is the **Crossplane** Upbound AWS provider API group (`Bucket`, plus separate `BucketVersioning`, `BucketServerSideEncryptionConfiguration`, `BucketPublicAccessBlock` managed resources).
- **ACK** uses `s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1`, where versioning/encryption/public-access-block are *inline fields on the single `Bucket` spec*, not separate objects.

Since the stack is described as ACK, I've written the below against `s3.services.k8s.aws` / `iam.services.k8s.aws`. If your cluster actually runs the Upbound provider, say so and I'll re-emit it as four separate managed resources with `spec.forProvider`.

Second correction: **there are no sensitive values in this feature.** A bucket name, an encryption algorithm, and a role ARN are all non-secret. Adding a SOPS-encrypted Secret here would be cargo-culting the existing pattern; the DB connection string in the spec is the thing that warrants SOPS. I've left SOPS out and noted where it *would* attach if you later add one.

## Layout

```
infra/s3/logs/          base bucket
infra/iam/logs/         IRSA role + policy
overlays/dev/logs/
overlays/prod/logs/
```

### `infra/s3/logs/bucket.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
spec:
  name: myapp-logs   # patched per-overlay
  versioning:
    status: Enabled
  encryption:
    rules:
      - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
          sseAlgorithm: AES256
        bucketKeyEnabled: true
  publicAccessBlock:
    blockPublicACLs: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicACLs: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
  ownershipControls:
    rules:
      - objectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced
```

### `infra/s3/logs/kustomization.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - bucket.yaml
```

### `infra/iam/logs/policy.yaml`

Least privilege, scoped to the one bucket, no wildcard actions:

```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-rw
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-rw
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Sid": "ListBucket",
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": ["s3:ListBucket", "s3:GetBucketLocation"],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs"
        },
        {
          "Sid": "ObjectRW",
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:GetObjectVersion",
            "s3:PutObject",
            "s3:DeleteObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs/*"
        }
      ]
    }
```

### `infra/iam/logs/role.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
spec:
  name: myapp-logs
  description: IRSA role for myapp logs bucket access
  maxSessionDuration: 3600
  assumeRolePolicyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Principal": {
            "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:oidc-provider/OIDC_ISSUER"
          },
          "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
          "Condition": {
            "StringEquals": {
              "OIDC_ISSUER:aud": "sts.amazonaws.com",
              "OIDC_ISSUER:sub": "system:serviceaccount:myapp:myapp-logs"
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  policyRefs:
    - from:
        name: myapp-logs-rw
```

Note the `sub` condition uses `StringEquals` on the exact service account, not `StringLike` with a wildcard — that's the difference between an IRSA role and an account-wide backdoor.

### `infra/iam/logs/serviceaccount.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
  namespace: myapp
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:role/myapp-logs
```

### `infra/iam/logs/kustomization.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - policy.yaml
  - role.yaml
  - serviceaccount.yaml
```

### `overlays/dev/logs/kustomization.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: myapp
resources:
  - ../../../infra/s3/logs
  - ../../../infra/iam/logs
nameSuffix: -dev
patches:
  - target: {kind: Bucket, name: myapp-logs}
    patch: |
      - op: replace
        path: /spec/name
        value: myapp-logs-dev
  - target: {kind: Policy, name: myapp-logs-rw}
    patch: |
      - op: replace
        path: /spec/name
        value: myapp-logs-rw-dev
  - target: {kind: Role, name: myapp-logs}
    patch: |
      - op: replace
        path: /spec/name
        value: myapp-logs-dev
```

Prod is the same with `-prod` and, if you want to mirror the assets bucket, an added replication block. **Caveat:** `nameSuffix` rewrites the k8s object names *and* fixes up `policyRefs.from.name` (it's a kustomize-aware ref only if you've registered a `nameReference` configuration for ACK CRDs). If you haven't, drop `nameSuffix` and give the dev/prod objects distinct `metadata.name` values via patches instead — silently unlinked `policyRefs` is the most likely way this breaks.

### `flux/kustomizations.yaml` — append

```yaml
---
apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
metadata:
  name: logs-dev
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 10m
  path: ./overlays/dev/logs
  prune: true
  sourceRef:
    kind: GitRepository
    name: flux-system      # must match the existing entries' sourceRef
  healthChecks:
    - apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
      kind: Bucket
      name: myapp-logs-dev
      namespace: myapp
```

…and an identical `logs-prod` block pointing at `./overlays/prod/logs`. Keeping these as separate Kustomizations per environment is what preserves the isolation criterion — a failing prod reconcile can't block dev.

## Two things to verify against your actual repo

I couldn't read the repo, so: (1) confirm the `sourceRef.name` — I assumed `flux-system`, but if your existing kustomizations point at a differently-named `GitRepository`, the new entries will fail with a source-not-found and nothing will reconcile. (2) Confirm ACK's IAM controller is installed and its `Role`/`Policy` CRDs are present; the S3 controller being present doesn't imply the IAM one is, and they're separate Helm installs with separate IRSA roles of their own.
